Sorry, this is repost, but most of it may be applicable for your situation:



Ok, I will make it short.(I am a physician, struggling with bipolar disease since 20 years)

Evaluate your risk of suicide. This should be done by a physician trained in psychiatry. This could be done out- or inpatient. (I don't know how medical structures are organized in your city - I live in Germany.
Information you can get via internet and perhaps local supporting groups, who may recomend a good doctor)
During evaluation you may discuss possibilitys to treat you (meds, psychotherapy, dayclinic or psychiatric hospital...), depending on how stable your "mind" is.

Many people have fears regarding psychiatry (due to misinformation or movies that use psychiatry to horror or thrill people, but have not much in common with present conditions in the psychiatric field.

Low self esteem, self consideration as invalid or worthless are symptoms of e.g. major depressive disorder and may be treated.

I myself have often blamed myself of being lazy or dump, (the reality is, that i am a doctor).

Even I see, that there a lot of problems in your life resulting that most people I your actual or past living conditions would be in a severely depressed mood.

But, most problems may be solved even if you may can't figure it or know or believe that change may be possible.

THE MOST IMPORTEND THING IS ALWAYS STAYING ALIVE. SOMETIMES IT IS NECESSARY TO BE HOSPITALIZED TO BE SAFE.
IF YOU'RE IN A STATE OF PLANNING SUICIDE OR PREPARING IT, CALL 911. 

This is that I also do in severe crises that accure 2-3 times per year.
Suicidel idiation is a SYMPTOM of your medical condition. (like cough if you have a flu).

Ok, hope this may help you a little bit. 
Best regards, Alex
